decisive_items: seven subcutaneous, nontender, mobile swellings measuring 1×1 to 3×3 cm in the cervical regions, right paraspinal area, and anterior abdominal wall
predominantly plump spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, fragments of collagenous matrix
Ultrasonography confirmed that all lesions were confined to the subcutaneous tissue, with no lymphadenopathy or deeper masses
response.rationale: Multiple subcutaneous, painless, mobile spindle-cell nodules with collagenous matrix and bland cytology in a teenager are most consistent with multiple neurofibromas; multiplicity makes neurofibromatosis type 1 the syndromic diagnosis, and absent family history does not exclude a de novo mutation.

rejected.why: Nodular fasciitis is typically solitary, painful, mitotically active, and inflammatory; these lesions are multiple, painless, and lack mitoses or inflammation.
Fibromatosis is usually a deep, infiltrative, solitary mass, not multiple mobile subcutaneous nodules.
Lipomatosis would show mature adipocytes on cytology, not plump spindle cells with collagenous matrix.
Hibernoma would show brown fat cells, not bland spindle cells, and is not typically multiple at these sites.
Elastofibroma is typically subscapular, solitary, and occurs in older patients.
Lipoma would show mature adipocytes, not spindle cells and collagenous matrix.
Neurofibroma is the lesion type, but the multiplicity of lesions favors the syndromic diagnosis of NF1.
Lymphoma would show lymphoid cells, not bland spindle cells, and US showed no lymphadenopathy.
DFSP is usually a solitary dermal tumor with more cellular storiform spindle cells, not multiple subcutaneous collagenous nodules.
